    {
      "login": "l0rinc",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Approach NACK; objects to exceptions due to unpredictable side effects and non-local control flow"
    },
    {
      "login": "furszy",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Objects to abrupt defect terminations that could corrupt wallet databases and risk user funds"
    },
    {
      "login": "ajtowns",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "NACK; argues exceptions introduce technical debt and contradict existing util::Expected/util::Result practice"
    },
    {
      "login": "maflcko",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Objects to merging as-is; raises review overhead and thread-shutdown deadlock concerns, and requests moving to developer-notes.md"
    },
    {
      "login": "josibake",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK; strongly agrees establishing a central error handling strategy is essential"
    },
    {
      "login": "willcl-ark",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK; supports having a well-defined error handling approach while inquiring about LLVM-style vs exceptions"
    },
    {
      "login": "mzumsande",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Objects to a global abort-on-defect policy, preferring domain-specific resilience patterns in P2P and RPC"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "r:5043038193",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Exceptions introduce unpredictable side-effects and invisible non-local control flow contrary to recent project direction.",
      "quote": "Approach NACK, instead of presenting your personal opinion as the only way forward, try gathering info first on the project's needs",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "contested",
      "status_note": "l0rinc pushed back arguing exceptions introduce non-local invisible control flow and calling throwing constructors a recipe for disaster.",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3873688067",
        "c:5442380284",
        "c:5460282324"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:5454791599",
      "status_by_quote": "An exception is an unannounced return value, it's a surprise, a side-effect: a lie."
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5044199538",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "Ungraceful process aborts on defects prevent graceful flushing and can leave the wallet database in an inconsistent or unrecoverable state, risking funds.",
      "quote": "There are multiple examples where abrupt terminations can cause the wallet to enter an inconsistent/unrecoverable state, which puts users' funds at risk.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "contested",
      "status_note": "furszy pushed back, arguing that a defect in one subsystem does not justify aborting without allowing other subsystems like the wallet to flush safely.",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5444749229",
        "c:5448269120"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:5446658393",
      "status_by_quote": "Only the affected subsystem should avoid flushing to disk. All others should be allowed to shut down gracefully."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5449877280",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Contradicts established codebase patterns like util::Expected and util::Result, introducing technical debt and worse error handling semantics.",
      "quote": "NACK, this isn't a problem that needs a 750 word essay to address... and the essay provided doesn't reflect existing practice (eg util/expected.h or util/result.h) so if merged would introduce signifi",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5450011864",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "Broad exception propagation forces reviewers to audit all calling threads and destructors for deadlock hazards during shutdown.",
      "quote": "If exceptions were used more broadly, reviewers must always implicitly consider all calling threads for all functions and waste review cycles on that",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5051185397",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "A global abort-on-defect directive breaks existing resilience patterns where non-consensus modules like P2P or RPC can handle bugs without node crashes.",
      "quote": "in p2p code that is triggerable remotely it is often best practice to add a debug-only Assume() and just abort the processing of the message, but not the entire program",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "contested",
      "status_note": "mzumsande pushed back, reiterating that a project-wide policy dictating defect handling outcomes is unacceptable given remote crash risks and defensive programming needs.",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5452864881",
        "c:5523137368"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:5526681542",
      "status_by_quote": "it is completely unacceptable to sacrifice any locally desired functional outcome in favor of nicer code or project-wide consistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5461033182",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "scope",
      "text": "The document creates internally contradictory documentation with existing utilities and belongs in doc/developer-notes.md rather than as a top-level document.",
      "quote": "it can absolutely not be merged in its current form, while ignoring the review feedback above. Merging it would create internally contradictory documentation. Also, doc/error-handling.md is the wrong ",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "author acknowledged refinement is needed in c:5461417690 but deferred actionable updates.",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5461417690"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5441565548",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Whether a failure to serialize should be categorized as a Result under the proposed strategy.",
      "quote": "Should a failure to serialize be what you call here a Result?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained that parsing untrusted network data fits into returning an optional/Result rather than throwing runtime errors.",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5442380284"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:5442380284",
      "status_by_quote": "Yes. Well, it depends on the contract of the function... Such a function would return std::optional<Block>, for example."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5442686187",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "What category unchecked exceptions like bad_alloc or standard library length errors and invalid arguments fit into under the proposal.",
      "quote": "Some of the code we call in the standard library does throw on length errors and invalid arguments. In what category do those fit in?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5451317733",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Whether the author considered the LLVM-style explicit-error-handling model and why exceptions are considered more appropriate for Bitcoin Core.",
      "quote": "I'd be interested to know whether you considered the LLVM-style approach in formulating this, and why you consider your approach as more appropriate for our project?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author replied detailing reasons why exceptions are preferred for Bitcoin Core over LLVM's approach.",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5452785466"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:5452785466",
      "status_by_quote": "The two reasons why exceptions are preferred for Bitcoin Core specifically are: A clear separation between Result and Error... The optimization for the success path."
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "c:5441565548",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "I think this is a good place to start off and matches close to my own ideal.",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "read",
      "areas": [
        "doc/error-handling.md"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5450114704",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "I strongly agree that an established error handling strategy is essential for a project of this size.",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "none",
      "areas": []
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5451317733",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "~ Concept ACK for having a more-well-defined approach to this for the project in general.",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "read",
      "areas": []
    }
  ],
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "author",
      "what": "author needs to respond to mzumsande's pushback on defect handling and decide whether to adapt the proposal",

    },

}
